To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we can learn a semantic space that captures the semantic composition of noun phrases from a corpus, and that (b) the semantic composition of a phrase can be predicted from brain activity, with a model trained to predict semantic properties of the phrase.

(1) the composition of words in corpora is consistent with the neural representation of meaning in the brain; and (2) the composition of adjective noun pairs in corpora is congruent with the composition of the same adjective noun pairs in the brain.

we have developed a new method for learning interpretable semantics from corpora, that we have developed new methods for combining brain data and corpus data into a joint model of word semantics, and that we have developed novel methods for analyzing semantic composition in brain data.
